actions: Ninetales used Fire Blast  // Drought is already up, so this Fire Blast is sun-boosted and 2x on Ice/Psychic. Jynx's Sash means it gets one action whatever I do, so I take the action that leaves it on 1 HP rather than the one that leaves me at +2 and asleep.
Jynx used Lovely Kiss  // Jynx outspeeds Ninetales at 161. Their sun is a fixed 8-turn clock, not a state I can dispel - so I make them spend it asleep. Focus Sash covers the 25% miss.

lines.text: Jynx hung on with its Focus Sash!

actions: switched to Arcanine  // Pivoting the sleeping Ninetales out resets its sleep counter, so the nap costs me one turn instead of three. Arcanine resists Ice Beam, brings Intimidate, and nothing on their roster resists a sun-boosted Choice Band Flare Blitz.
Jynx used Psychic  // Jynx is a dead body walking at 1 HP, so I spend its last action on damage. Psychic hits a sleeping Ninetales for ~58% and is 2x on Venusaur or Victreebel if they pivot.

Arcanine used Extreme Speed  // Jynx outspeeds and its Psychic already did 99 to a 67-HP Arcanine, so any non-priority move loses Arcanine for nothing. Extreme Speed at +2 removes their fastest special attacker and their only sleep move before it can fire again.

Jynx used Psychic  // Arcanine at 39% is inside Psychic's roll. Trading a 1 HP Jynx whose Lovely Kiss is sleep-clause-locked for a Choice Band sun attacker is a bargain even if Extreme Speed beats me to it.

switched to Gengar  // Choice Band has locked Arcanine into Extreme Speed, a Normal move. Gengar is immune to Normal, so it enters for free and threatens to OHKO whatever they pivot to with Sludge Wave.

switched to Venusaur  // Extreme Speed is a 0x into a Ghost and I'm Choice-locked, so staying is a free turn for them. Venusaur is the one switch-in a status team cannot break: immune to Toxic and poison, and burn barely dents a special attacker. Chlorophyll puts it at 264 Speed in this sun, faster than Gengar.

Gengar used Sludge Wave  // Sludge Wave covers every branch: it kills a 39% Arcanine if it stays, and it is 2x on Venusaur, Victreebel and Exeggutor - three of their five remaining bodies - hitting them the instant they switch in.

lines.text: Gengar was hurt by its Life Orb! (-13)

actions: Venusaur used Sleep Powder  // Venusaur at 33 dies to the next Sludge Wave regardless, so I spend its last action on the biggest swing available. Chlorophyll has me at 264 vs Gengar's 178, so Sleep Powder goes first: a 75% shot at deleting their fastest attacker and buying Exeggutor a free entry to Psychic it.

Gengar used Sludge Wave  // Venusaur at 21% is dead to another Sludge Wave, and Gengar resists both its STABs at 0.5x - Chlorophyll outspeeding me does not matter when nothing it throws can break 123 HP.

switched to Ninetales  // My predecessor lost this team's whole identity by never getting the sun back. Gengar asleep is the safest reset window I will get: Ninetales re-triggers Drought for 8 turns off Heat Rock, wakes on entry because the earlier pivot zeroed its sleep counter, and is then in range to Fire Blast the napping Gengar.

switched to Golbat  // A sleeping Gengar is a free Growth for Venusaur, and +2 breaks even the resisted hit. Golbat takes Grass at 0.25x and Poison at 0.5x - Venusaur literally cannot dent it - and Air Slash is 2x to finish a 21% body.

Ninetales used Nasty Plot  // Golbat is a Roost + Sitrus pivot, so two 116-damage Fire Blasts lose to its recovery while one +2 Fire Blast (~232) does not. Golbat's answer to me is Toxic, not damage, so the setup turn is cheap. Ninetales outspeeds it 167 to 110 and cashes the boost next turn while the sun is still up.

Golbat used Poison Fang  // Ninetales is asleep and cannot punish me, so I spend the free turn on Poison Fang's 50% bad-poison roll. Putting the Drought setter on a permanent clock is what caps their sun at this one dying cycle.

Ninetales used Fire Blast  // Last turn of sun and the boost is live: +2 STAB Fire Blast in sunlight is roughly 232 into a ~160 HP Golbat, which overruns both Sitrus and Roost in one action. Cash it now — next turn the sky goes out and the same move drops to ~155.

Golbat used Confuse Ray  // A +2 sun Fire Blast OHKOs every body I own, so I am losing one this turn no matter what - switching would only waste the action too. Golbat is my most redundant wall, so it stays and buys the 15% branch where Fire Blast misses and a +2 Ninetales ends up confused.

switched to Gengar  // Gengar switched out asleep, which zeroes its sleep counter - it is guaranteed to wake on its first move attempt and still act, exactly as their Ninetales did on turn 7. It outspeeds 178 to 167 and Sludge Wave kills a +2 Ninetales before it can fire again.

switched to Victreebel  // Gengar's sleep counter was zeroed by its own switch-out, so it wakes and moves first at 178 to my 167 — Sludge Wave is a coin-flip to kill Ninetales and I will not gamble the only Drought on my team. Victreebel's Focus Sash guarantees it lives the hit, and Sucker Punch is Dark and 2x back, which after Life Orb recoil is lethal on Gengar.

Gengar used Sludge Wave  // Gengar wakes on this move attempt and moves first at 178 speed. Sludge Wave rolls 108-127 into Ninetales' 111 HP - killing the Drought setter ends any chance of a second sun and erases the +2 in one action.

lines.text: Victreebel hung on with its Focus Sash!
Gengar was hurt by its Life Orb! (-13)

actions: Victreebel used Sucker Punch  // The only move that resolves before a 178-Speed Gengar. Sucker Punch is Dark into a Ghost for ~136 against its ~107 remaining, so it kills on every roll if Gengar attacks — and if Gengar instead clicks a status move, Sucker Punch whiffs but Victreebel takes zero damage. There is no line where this loses me anything.

Gengar used Sludge Wave  // Their switch threw away the +2 Nasty Plot entirely. Off-sun Gengar's 178 outruns their whole roster, and Sludge Wave now kills Victreebel, Venusaur, Arcanine, Exeggutor or Ninetales - five of six switch-ins die to this one click.

switched to Arbok  // Arbok resists both Victreebel STABs, Intimidate halves it, and Rocky Helmet's 26 chip kills a 1 HP Victreebel on any contact move - Sucker Punch and Power Whip both make contact, so it dies whichever it picks.

switched to Ninetales  // Sun has actually lapsed now, so Drought will really fire this time. Arbok is the safest thing on their roster to re-enter against — Intimidate/Rocky Helmet/Glare, base 65 SpA, no real damage. I need the sky back before Zapdos arrives: unsunned Charizard does ~99 to Zapdos and Roost heals 99, which is a stalemate I lose. Sunned it does ~223.

Arbok used Glare  // Glare is a status move, so Victreebel's Sucker Punch fails outright and Power Whip just kills it on my Rocky Helmet. If they pivot instead, the paralysis lands on the switch-in - and halving speed is how I dismantle a team whose whole creed is being fastest.

Ninetales used Fire Blast  // Ninetales is already paralysed, which makes it status-proof — Arbok's Glare has nothing left to do here. That makes it the right body to grind Arbok down with, and it keeps Glare away from Charizard, whose 167-to-120 speed edge over Zapdos is the whole endgame. Sun Fire Blast chips ~126 and shows me Arbok's attacking move.

Arbok used Earthquake  // My own Glare bought this: paralysis drops Ninetales to 83 and Arbok's 100 now moves first. Earthquake is 2x into Fire and rolls 119-140 into 111 HP - a guaranteed kill on the Drought engine, so this third sun is their last.

switched to Exeggutor  // Exeggutor is the hard answer to what just killed me: Grass resists Ground, so Earthquake drops from a 2x kill to a 0.5x scratch. Chlorophyll puts it at 214 over Arbok's ~100, Psychic is 2x into a pure Poison-type, and it is non-contact so Rocky Helmet never gets to bite back.

Exeggutor used Psychic  // Psychic into a pure Poison-type at 2x, from 214 Speed so it lands before Arbok can move. This should remove the Earthquake that just took my sun setter, and it costs Exeggutor nothing on the return since Ground is resisted and Psychic avoids Rocky Helmet.

switched to Zapdos  // Exeggutor's Psychic is 2x on Poison and OHKOs Arbok from behind Chlorophyll speed, so Arbok cannot stay. Zapdos eats Grass at 0.25x and Psychic for only ~108 of 197, and it is the body that answers Charizard, Venusaur and Victreebel too.
